preregistration.summary: Today 12/10/2026. Contract 01/09/2020 signed by the two representatives only, no witnesses; six installments of R$30,000 due the 10th of Oct/2020..Mar/2021. CPC 784 III requires two witnesses and the library states boleto is not a title, so execution is barred; the route is monitoria (CPC 700) or cobranca. Prescription is 5 years (CC 206 s5 I) from each due date: original terms 2025-10-10, 2025-11-10, 2025-12-10, 2026-01-10, 2026-02-10, 2026-03-10. The 15/09/2022 e-mail recognises installments 1-4 only and expressly contests 5-6; it is the single permitted interruption (CC 202 caput, VI, par. unico), so 1-4 restart to 2027-09-15. The 02/08/2023 PIX of R$10,000 'por conta da parcela 1' is a new recognition but cannot interrupt again. Installments 5-6 never interrupted: prescribed 2026-02-10 and 2026-03-10, before the 12/08/2026 Serasa listing. Exigible principal 4x30,000 - 10,000 = 110,000; prescribed 60,000. Serasa listing of 180,000 = 110,000 exigible + 60,000 prescribed + 10,000 already paid. Three prior uncontested listings (2024-25) trigger Sumula 385: no moral damages, but cancellation/rectification is still due. Protest (Lei 9.492) only of exigible debt; never of 5-6. Rough charges on 1-4 to today at 1% a.m. simple plus 2% fine: about R$82k interest + R$2.2-2.4k fine, no IPCA series in the pack.

cross_run_observations: All five runs reached the same core answers without prompting: monitoria instead of execution, installments 1-4 alive until 2027-09-15, 5-6 prescribed on 2026-02-10 and 2026-03-10, exigible principal R$110,000, R$60,000 prescribed, rectify the Serasa listing, never protest 5-6, Sumula 385 mitigates damages but cancellation is due. All five answered the pushback with the single-interruption rule of CC 202 caput and the library's own note that the later partial payment does not re-interrupt. No run cited anything outside library/INDEX.md in its final deliverables; B, D and E each caught and relabelled off-library statements during their review turns. The one systematic oracle miss is negativacao.indevida_quanto_a: every run answered 70,000 (prescribed 60,000 plus the 10,000 already paid), while the key expects 60,000; this looks like a key ambiguity rather than five independent errors and is flagged as a fixture issue. Interest estimates differ only by day-count convention (A: 81,990 with fine on reduced balance -> 194,190; B: months+days/30 -> 193,256.67; C/D/E: days/30 -> 194,390); all reconcile with independent recomputation. No run invented an IPCA series; all left correction monetaria open. Three runs (A, B, C) did not ask about witnesses because the contract document already states 'Sem testemunhas'; D and E asked anyway. D's chat summary (not its deliverables) contained a wrong prescription period ('3 anos, CC 206 s3 I') and a phantom 'Fiador Ltda.' reference; no trust-fatal event was recorded because the deliverables are correct, but it is noted.
